system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:51 UTC, Zeek recorded 50,000,468 bytes sent from WS-MLOPEZ-01 to the explicit proxy at 10.30.20.30:8080 over about 15 seconds. The record does not identify the external destination, application, or content.

At 14:17 UTC, Maria Lopez's browser connected through the proxy to drive.google.com; the recorded client-to-server tunnel volume was 1,230 bytes. This does not establish that the large transfer went to Google Drive or that data was uploaded there.

A UserAssist registry entry updated at 13:22 contains a ROT13-encoded path that decodes to Windows PowerShell. This suggests PowerShell was used, but does not establish what commands ran or whether that activity caused the later transfer.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied sensor coverage status reports a collection outage from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC for WS-MLOPEZ-01 winsec and Sysmon, and for the proxy. The large transfer at 13:51 falls within this gap.
Zeek connection and DNS coverage is reported as available, but the transfer record identifies only the workstation-to-proxy connection, not its external destination or payload.
claims_not_established: The external destination, URL, service, and recipient of the 50 MB transfer.
The process or user action that generated the transfer, and whether it was an upload, a legitimate application transaction, or malicious exfiltration.
Whether the transfer contained sensitive or otherwise unauthorized data.
Whether the PowerShell-related UserAssist entry is connected to the transfer.
Whether the later Google Drive connection was related to the large transfer.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover proxy logs or upstream network records for 13:30–14:10 UTC to identify the destination, request method, and transfer details.

Collect endpoint telemetry or forensic artifacts for WS-MLOPEZ-01 covering the outage, including process execution, browser history/download/upload artifacts, file access, and relevant PowerShell logs.
Establish the source and contents of the transferred data and confirm with Maria Lopez or the relevant business owner whether the activity was authorized.
